# 4 Maccabees Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Antiochus and the Jerusalem Temple

---

**1** During the reign of Seleucus Nicanor over Asia, a man named Simon, who administered the temple, got into a dispute with Onias the high priest over the management of the city marketplace.

**2** He could not win the argument, so Simon went to Apollonius son of Thraseas, the regional governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.

**3** He told Apollonius that the Jerusalem temple treasury was overflowing with enormous wealth — more deposits than could be counted — and that these funds were not temple revenues at all, but private holdings of Ptolemy son of Seleucus, a powerful man.

**4** Apollonius was thrilled by the news and went straight to King Antiochus with the report.

**5** Given royal authorization, Apollonius went to Judea with the treacherous Simon and Menelaus.

**6** He announced that by royal decree all these funds were to be seized for the king's treasury.

**7** Onias the high priest, though loyal to the king, stood before his people and refused to go along with this, saying:

**8** We cannot hand over the sacred deposits to the king. These funds belong to God.

**9** But Simon, acting like a criminal, slipped into the sanctuary while Onias was away and helped himself to some of the sacred offerings for the king's treasury.

**10** Antiochus himself then came to Jerusalem, having been tipped off by the treacherous Simon that the treasury was packed with riches.

**11** He announced: adopt Greek customs or I will execute everyone in this land.

**12** When he found that the whole population would rather die than abandon their ancestral faith, he went to the temple himself to plunder it.

**13** Onias the temple's guardian cried out to God: Lord, you know I have kept faith with your law — protect your holy place!

**14** Antiochus walked right in, and his men came with him to strip the sacred vessels.

**15** But the God who watches everything and punishes the wicked struck Antiochus down on the spot.

**16** He was suddenly struck blind and collapsed; his companions were seized with terror as God's darkness covered the sanctuary.

**17** But in his pride Antiochus pushed on even into the inner sanctuary.

**18** He stripped the temple of the golden altar, the menorah, the table for the sacred bread, the libation vessels, the incense burners, the great curtain, and all the ornamental decorations.

**19** He took everything. He left with enormous arrogance.

**20** He then appointed Jason as high priest — a completely lawless and corrupt man.

**21** Jason had offered a bribe of three hundred sixty talents of silver, promising that if he got the position he would force the people to adopt Greek culture.

**22** Jason was installed as high priest and immediately began pushing his people toward Greek ways of living.

**23** He abolished the ancestral laws and introduced customs directly contrary to the law.

**24** He built a gymnasium right at the foot of the temple citadel and persuaded the most prominent young men to wear the Greek broad-brimmed hat.

**25** Through the sheer wickedness of the ungodly Jason, Greek customs spread everywhere and foreign practices took over.

**26** The priests lost all interest in serving at the altar; they neglected the sacrifices and deserted the sanctuary to take part in athletic competitions.
